title: 源氏物語
author: 紫式部（日本・平安時代）
source: Retold in simple Japanese by Claude (N2 level)

sentences.en: Chapter 1: The Shining Prince

sentences.jp: 平安時代、ある天皇が、身分の高くない桐壺更衣という女性を深く愛していた。
sentences.en: In the Heian period, an emperor deeply loved a woman of not very high rank, Lady Kiritsubo.

sentences.jp: ほかの女性たちのねたみを受け、更衣は病気になり、男の子を産んでまもなく亡くなった。
sentences.en: Resented by the other women, she fell ill and died soon after giving birth to a son.

sentences.jp: その子はとても美しく、才能にあふれていたので、「光る君」と呼ばれた。
sentences.en: The boy was so beautiful and gifted that he was called "the Shining Prince."

sentences.jp: しかし強い後ろだてがなかったため、天皇は彼を皇族からはずし、「源」という姓を与えた。
sentences.en: But because he had no powerful backers, the emperor removed him from the imperial family and gave him the surname Minamoto (Genji).

sentences.jp: こうして彼は、光源氏と呼ばれるようになった。
sentences.en: And so he came to be called Hikaru Genji.

sentences.h: 第二章　かなわぬ恋
sentences.en: Chapter 2: A love that cannot be

sentences.jp: 天皇は、亡き更衣にそっくりな藤壺という女性を新しい妃に迎えた。
sentences.en: The emperor took as a new consort a woman named Fujitsubo, who looked just like the late Lady Kiritsubo.

sentences.jp: 母の顔を知らない源氏は、藤壺を慕い、やがて恋をしてしまう。
sentences.en: Genji, who never knew his mother's face, adored Fujitsubo and eventually fell in love with her.

sentences.jp: それは父の妃への、決して許されない恋だった。
sentences.en: It was a forbidden love for his own father's consort.

sentences.jp: 源氏は多くの女性と恋をしたが、心の中にはいつも藤壺がいた。
sentences.en: Genji had love affairs with many women, but Fujitsubo was always in his heart.

sentences.jp: 二人の間には、ひそかに男の子が生まれ、その子はのちに天皇になる。
sentences.en: A son was secretly born to the two of them, and that child would later become emperor.
Chapter 3: Murasaki

sentences.jp: ある春、源氏は山寺で、藤壺によく似た十歳ほどの少女を見つけた。
sentences.en: One spring, at a mountain temple, Genji found a girl of about ten who closely resembled Fujitsubo.

sentences.jp: 少女は藤壺の姪だった。
sentences.en: The girl was Fujitsubo's niece.

sentences.jp: 源氏は彼女を自分の屋敷に引き取り、理想の女性に育てた。
sentences.en: Genji took her into his mansion and raised her to be his ideal woman.

sentences.jp: この少女がのちの紫の上で、源氏の一生で最も大切な人となった。
sentences.en: This girl was the later Lady Murasaki, who became the most important person in Genji's life.

sentences.h: 第四章　須磨への旅
sentences.en: Chapter 4: Exile to Suma

sentences.jp: 源氏は敵の一族の娘と恋をしたことが知られ、都にいられなくなった。
sentences.en: When it became known that Genji had an affair with a daughter of a rival clan, he could no longer stay in the capital.

sentences.jp: 彼は自分から須磨の海辺へ下り、寂しい日々を送った。
sentences.en: He withdrew of his own accord to the seashore at Suma and spent lonely days there.

sentences.jp: そこで明石の君という女性と出会い、娘が生まれた。
sentences.en: There he met a woman, the Lady of Akashi, and a daughter was born.

sentences.jp: やがて都に呼び戻されると、源氏は以前よりも高い地位にのぼっていった。
sentences.en: Eventually he was called back to the capital and rose to an even higher position than before.

sentences.h: 第五章　栄華と孤独
sentences.en: Chapter 5: Glory and loneliness

sentences.jp: 源氏は広大な屋敷、六条院を建て、愛する女性たちをそこに住まわせた。
sentences.en: Genji built a vast mansion, the Rokujō-in, and had the women he loved live there.

sentences.jp: 娘は天皇の后になり、源氏の栄華は頂点に達した。
sentences.en: His daughter became the emperor's consort, and Genji's glory reached its peak.

sentences.jp: しかし年をとると、若い妻が別の男と通じ、子どもが生まれた。
sentences.en: But as he grew old, his young wife had an affair with another man, and a child was born.

sentences.jp: 源氏は、かつて自分が父にしたことが、自分に返ってきたと感じた。
sentences.en: Genji felt that what he had once done to his father had come back to him.

sentences.jp: やがて最愛の紫の上が病気で亡くなった。
sentences.en: Before long, his beloved Murasaki died of illness.

sentences.jp: 源氏は深い悲しみの中で出家を決意し、物語の舞台から静かに姿を消す。
sentences.en: In deep grief, Genji resolved to become a monk and quietly disappears from the story.

sentences.jp: 物語は、その後の子どもや孫の世代へと続いていく。
sentences.en: The tale goes on to the generations of his children and grandchildren.
